abandon.def: To give up or relinquish control of, to surrender or to give oneself over, or to yield to one's emotions.

abolish.def: To end a law, system, institution, custom or practice.

abrupt.def: Without notice to prepare the mind for the event; sudden; hasty; unceremonious.

absence.def: A state of being away or withdrawn from a place or from companionship

accelerate.def: To cause to move faster; to quicken the motion of; to add to the speed of.

accompany.def: To go with or attend as a companion or associate; to keep company with; to go along with.

accountable.def: Obliged, when called upon, to answer (for one’s deeds); answerable.

accumulate.def: To gradually grow or increase in quantity or number.

achieve.def: To carry out successfully; to accomplish.

adequate.def: Equal to or fulfilling some requirement.

adherent.def: A person who has membership in some group, association, or religion.

admiration.def: A positive emotion including wonder and approbation; the regarding of another as being wonderful

adore.def: To love with one's entire heart and soul; regard with deep respect and affection.

adverse.def: Unfavorable; antagonistic in purpose or effect; hostile; actively opposing one's interests or wishes; contrary to one's welfare; acting against; working in an opposing direction.

alien.def: A citizen or national of another sovereign state.

alike.def: Having resemblance or similitude; similar; without difference.

ally.def: A person who co-operates with or helps another; an associate; a friend.

alter.def: To change the form or structure of.

anguish.def: Extreme pain, either of body or mind; excruciating distress.

announcement.def: An act of announcing, or giving notice.

anonymously.def: In an anonymous manner; without a name.

anticipate.def: To know of (something) before it happens; to expect.

appeal.def: To call upon someone for a favour, help, etc.

appreciation.def: A fair valuation or estimate of merit, worth, weight, etc.; recognition of excellence; gratitude and esteem.

apprehend.def: To take hold of (something) with understanding; to conceive (something) in the mind; to become cognizant of; to understand.

aptitude.def: Natural ability to acquire knowledge or skill.

arbitrary.def: Based on individual discretion or judgment; not based on any objective distinction, perhaps even made at random.

arduous.def: Needing or using up much energy; testing powers of endurance.

arise.def: To come up from one's bed or place of repose; to get up.

arrogant.def: Having excessive pride in oneself, often with contempt or disrespect for others.

article.def: A piece of nonfiction writing such as a story, report, opinion piece, or entry in a newspaper, magazine, journal, encyclopedia, etc.

artificial.def: Man-made; made by humans; of artifice.

ascend.def: To move upward, to fly, to soar.

aspect.def: Any specific feature, part, or element of something.

aspire.def: To have a strong desire or ambition to achieve something.

assimilate.def: To incorporate or absorb (knowledge) into the mind.

associate.def: To join in or form a league, union, or association.

barren.def: Of poor fertility, infertile; not producing vegetation; desert, waste.

basis.def: A starting point, base or foundation for an argument or hypothesis.

bearable.def: Able to be borne; tolerable; endurable.

benefit.def: An advantage; help or aid from something.

beware.def: To use caution, pay attention to (used both with and without of).

bilingual.def: Having the ability to speak two languages fluently.

blossom.def: To have, or open into, blossoms; to bloom.

boom.def: A low-pitched, resonant sound, such as of an explosion.

breakdown.def: A failure, particularly one which is mechanical in nature.

breezy.def: With a breeze blowing, with a lively wind, pleasantly windy.

brink.def: The edge, margin, or border of a steep place, as of a precipice; a bank or edge.

broadly.def: Broadly speaking; in a wide manner; liberally; in a loose sense.

budget.def: The amount of money or resources earmarked for a particular institution, activity or timeframe.

candidate.def: A person who seeks to be elected or appointed to a position or privilege.

cherish.def: To treat with affection, care, and tenderness; to nurture or protect with care.

conscious.def: Alert, awake; with one's mental faculties active.

courteous.def: Showing regard or thought for others; especially, displaying good manners or etiquette.

cue.def: The name of the Latin-script letter Q/q.

domestic.def: Of or relating to the home.

empirical.def: Pertaining to or based on experience, as opposed to theory.

enhance.def: To augment or make something greater.

ensure.def: To make sure or certain of something (usually some future event or condition).

envious.def: Feeling or exhibiting envy; jealously desiring the excellence or good fortune of another; maliciously grudging.

equivalent.def: Similar or identical in value, meaning or effect; virtually equal.

eradicate.def: To destroy completely; to reduce to nothing radically; to put an end to.

erect.def: To put up by the fitting together of materials or parts.

erosion.def: The result of having been worn away or eroded, as by a glacier on rock or the sea on a cliff face.

refugee.def: A person seeking refuge (as for shelter or protection), especially in a foreign country, out of fear or prospect of political, religious persecution, war, natural disaster, etc.

refute.def: To prove (something) to be false or incorrect.

regard.def: One's concern for another; esteem; relation, reference.

register.def: To enter in a register; to enlist.

regret.def: To feel sorry about (a thing that has or has not happened), afterthink: to wish that a thing had not happened, that something else had happened instead.

regrettably.def: In a manner inspiring or deserving regret.

regulation.def: A law or administrative rule, issued by an organization, used to guide or prescribe the conduct of members of that organization.

rehearsal.def: The practising of something which is to be performed before an audience, usually to test or improve the interaction between several participating people, or to allow technical adjustments with respect to staging to be done.

reign.def: To exercise sovereign power, to rule as a monarch.

reinforce.def: To strengthen, especially by addition or augmentation.

reject.def: To refuse to accept; to forswear.

relevant.def: Related, connected, or pertinent to a topic.

reliable.def: Suitable or fit to be relied on; worthy of dependence, reliance or trust; dependable, trustworthy

reluctantly.def: In a reluctant or hesitant manner.

remark.def: A casual observation, comment, or statement

remedy.def: A medicine, application, or treatment that relieves or cures a disease.

remind.def: To cause one to experience a memory (of someone or something); to bring to the notice or consideration (of a person).

reminiscent.def: Suggestive of an earlier event or times.

remnant.def: A small portion remaining of a larger thing or group; part of a former whole.

repetitive.def: Happening many times in a similar way; containing repetition; repeating.

replace.def: To supply or substitute an equivalent with.

representative.def: Typical; having the same properties or interest as a larger group.

reputation.def: What somebody or something is known for.

require.def: Naturally to demand (something) as indispensable; to need, to call for as necessary.

resemble.def: To be like or similar to (something); to represent as similar.

resentful.def: Harboring resentment, full of resentment, at a given moment.

residence.def: The place where one lives (resides); one's home.

resist.def: To oppose; to refuse to accept.

resort.def: To have recourse (to), now especially from necessity or frustration.

respectively.def: In a relative manner; often used when comparing array lists, where the term denotes that the items in the lists correspond to each other in the order they are given.

response.def: An answer or reply, or something in the nature of an answer or reply.

restless.def: Without rest; unable to be still or quiet; uneasy; continually moving.

restore.def: To reestablish, or bring back into existence.

restrain.def: To control or keep in check.

restrict.def: To restrain within boundaries; to limit; to confine

resume.def: To start (something) again that has been stopped or paused from the point at which it was stopped or paused; continue, carry on.

retain.def: Often followed by from: to hold back (someone or something); to check, to prevent, to restrain, to stop.

retreat.def: The act of pulling back or withdrawing, as from something dangerous, or unpleasant.

reveal.def: To uncover; to show and display that which was hidden.

revenue.def: The total income received from a given source.

revise.def: To review, alter and amend, especially of written material.

revival.def: The act of reviving, or the state of being revived.

reward.def: To give a reward to or for.

rhyme.def: To compose or treat in verse; versify.

rigorous.def: Showing, causing, or favoring rigour/rigor; scrupulously accurate or strict; thorough.

ripe.def: Of a fruit, vegetable, seed, etc., ready for reaping or gathering; having attained perfection; mature.

ritual.def: A rite; a repeated set of actions, especially in religious contexts.

rival.def: A competitor (person, team, company, etc.) with the same goal as another, or striving to attain the same thing. Defeating a rival may be a primary or necessary goal of a competitor.

roam.def: To wander or travel freely and with no specific destination.

roar.def: Of animals (especially a lion), to make a loud deep noise.

robust.def: Evincing strength and health; strong; (often, especially) both large and healthy.

root.def: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.

rotten.def: Of perishable items, overridden with bacteria and other infectious agents.

roughly.def: Without precision or exactness; imprecisely but close to in quantity or amount; approximately.

routinely.def: In a routine manner, in a way that has become common or expected.

royal.def: Of or relating to a monarch or his (or her) family.

ruin.def: Something that leads to serious trouble or destruction.

rumour.def: British, Canada, New Zealand, Australia, and Ireland spelling of rumor.

ruthless.def: Without pity or compassion; cruel, pitiless.

sack.def: To put in a sack or sacks.

sacrifice.def: (religion) To offer (a human being or an animal, or an object) to a deity.

scale.def: An ordered, usually numerical sequence used for measurement; means of assigning a magnitude.

scarce.def: Uncommon, rare; difficult to find; insufficient to meet a demand.

scarcely.def: Hardly: only just; by a small margin.

scene.def: The location of an event that attracts attention.

schedule.def: A procedural plan, usually but not necessarily tabular in nature, indicating a sequence of operations and the planned times at which those operations are to occur.

scheme.def: A systematic plan of future action.

scholar.def: A student; one who studies at school or college, typically having a scholarship.

scratch.def: To rub a surface with a sharp object, especially by a living creature to remove itching with nails, claws, etc.

secular.def: Not specifically religious; lay or civil, as opposed to clerical.

seek.def: To try to find; to look for; to search for.

seize.def: To deliberately take hold of; to grab or capture.

sensation.def: A physical feeling or perception from something that comes into contact with the body; something sensed.

sensible.def: Acting with or showing good sense; able to make good judgements based on reason or wisdom, or reflecting such ability.

setback.def: An obstacle, delay, disadvantage, or blow (an adverse event which slows down, or prevents progress towards a desired outcome).

settlement.def: A community of people living together, such as a hamlet, village, town, or city; a populated place.

shallow.def: Having little depth; significantly less deep than wide.

shiver.def: To tremble or shake, especially when cold or frightened.

sigh.def: To inhale a larger quantity of air than usual, and immediately expel it; to make a deep single audible respiration, especially as the result or involuntary expression of fatigue, exhaustion, grief, sorrow, frustration, or the like.

skip.def: To move by hopping on alternate feet.

slaughter.def: To butcher animals, generally for food.

slightly.def: To a small extent or degree.

smooth.def: Having a texture that lacks friction. Not rough.

snack.def: An item of food eaten between meals.

soar.def: To fly high with little effort, like a bird.

solidarity.def: A bond of unity or agreement between individuals, united around a common goal or against a common enemy, such as the unifying principle that defines the labor movement; mutual support within a group.

solitary.def: Living or being by oneself; alone; having no companion present

sophisticated.def: Of a person: having obtained worldly experience, and lacking naiveté; cosmopolitan, worldly-wise.

spacious.def: Having plenty of space; roomy; capacious.

span.def: The full width of an open hand from the end of the thumb to the end of the little finger used as an informal unit of length.

spark.def: To give off a spark or sparks.

spectator.def: One who observes, sees, or views something; an observer.

speculate.def: To make an inference based on inconclusive evidence; to surmise or conjecture.

spill.def: To drop something so that it spreads out or makes a mess; to accidentally pour.

spin.def: To rotate, revolve, gyrate (usually quickly); to partially or completely rotate to face another direction.

splendid.def: Gorgeous; magnificent; sumptuous; of remarkable beauty.

split.def: To divide fully or partly along a more or less straight line.

spoil.def: To ruin; to damage in such a way as to make undesirable or unusable.

spontaneous.def: Self-generated; happening without any apparent external cause.

spot.def: To see, find; to pick out, notice, locate, distinguish or identify.

spy.def: A person who secretly watches and examines the actions of other individuals or organizations and gathers information on them (usually to gain an advantage).

stamina.def: The energy and strength for continuing to do something over a long period of time; power of sustained exertion, or resistance to hardship, illness etc.

staple.def: Relating to, or being market of staple for, commodities.

startle.def: To excite by sudden alarm, surprise, or apprehension; to frighten suddenly and not seriously; to alarm; to surprise.

starvation.def: A condition of severe suffering due to a lack of nutrition.

state.def: To declare to be a fact.

steady.def: Constant in feeling, purpose, or pursuit; not fickle, changeable, or wavering; not easily moved or persuaded to alter a purpose; resolute.

steep.def: Of a near-vertical gradient; of a slope, surface, curve, etc. that proceeds upward at an angle near vertical.

strain.def: A particular variety of a microbe, virus, or other organism, usually a taxonomically infraspecific one.

strike.def: A status resulting from a batter swinging and missing a pitch, or not swinging at a pitch when the ball goes in the strike zone, or hitting a foul ball that is not caught.

stuff.def: Miscellaneous items or objects; (with possessive) personal effects.

substitute.def: To use in place of something else, with the same function.

succeed.def: To prevail in obtaining an intended objective or accomplishment; to prosper as a result or conclusion of a particular effort.

successively.def: In a serial or successive manner; one following another.

sufficient.def: Of a type or kind that suffices, that satisfies requirements or needs.

suffocate.def: To suffer, or cause someone to suffer, from severely reduced oxygen intake to the body.

summit.def: The highest point of a hill, mountain, or similar geographical feature.

summon.def: To call people together; to convene; to convoke.

superficial.def: Appearing to be true or real only until examined more closely.

superior.def: Higher in rank, status, or quality.

supervise.def: To oversee or direct a task or organization.

suppress.def: To put an end to, especially with force, to crush, do away with; to prohibit, subdue.

surpass.def: To go beyond or exceed (something) in an adjudicative or literal sense.

surrender.def: To give oneself up into the power of another, especially as a prisoner; to submit or give in.

surroundings.def: The area surrounding someone or something, together with the objects and circumstances in the vicinity; the environment or ambiance.

survey.def: A particular view; an examination, especially an official examination, of a particular group of items, in order to ascertain the condition, quantity, or quality.

suspiciously.def: In a way that arouses suspicion.

sustain.def: To maintain, or keep in existence.

swear.def: To use offensive, profane, or obscene language.

sweep.def: To clean (a surface) by means of a stroking motion of a broom or brush.

swiftly.def: In a swift manner; quickly; with quick motion or velocity; fleetly.

tackle.def: To force a person to the ground with the weight of one's own body, usually by jumping on top or slamming one's weight into them.

tax.def: Money or goods collected by a government (or an entity to whom the government has delegated this power, e.g. in tax farming) to fund itself and its services, for example by levying a charge on income, purchases (sales), property or harvest, other than that money which is collected by the government in exchange for specific goods (e.g. the purchase of surplus vehicles).

temper.def: A general tendency or orientation towards a certain type of mood, a volatile state; a habitual way of thinking, behaving or reacting.

temporary.def: Not permanent; existing only for a period or periods of time.

temptation.def: Something attractive, tempting or seductive; an inducement, seducement, or enticement.

tendency.def: A likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction; a tending toward.

tender.def: Sensitive or painful to the touch.

tension.def: The condition of being held in a state between two or more forces, which are acting in opposition to each other.

terminate.def: To end something, especially when left in an incomplete state.

territory.def: A large extent or tract of land; for example a region, country or district.

theme.def: A subject, now especially of a talk or an artistic piece; a topic.

thoroughly.def: In a thorough or complete manner.

threatening.def: Presenting a threat, posing a likely risk of harm.

threshold.def: The lowermost part of a doorway that one crosses to enter; a sill.

thrive.def: To increase in wealth or success; to prosper, be profitable.

tip.def: The extreme end of something, especially when pointed; e.g. the sharp end of a pencil.

tissue.def: A sheet of absorbent paper, especially one that is made to be used as tissue paper, toilet paper or a handkerchief.

tomb.def: A small building, or a room within one, for the remains of the dead, with walls, a roof, and (if it is to be used for more than one corpse) a door. It may be partly or wholly in the ground (except for its entrance) in a cemetery, or it may be inside a church proper or in its crypt. Single tombs may be permanently sealed; those for families (or other groups) have doors for access whenever needed.

torture.def: The infliction of severe pain or anguish, especially as an interrogation technique or punishment; (usually in the plural) a technique, method, or device which is designed to inflict such anguish.

trait.def: An identifying characteristic, habit or trend.

transition.def: The process of change from one form, state, style or place to another.

transmit.def: To communicate (news or information, especially electronically).

transparent.def: See-through, clear; having the property that light passes through it almost undisturbed, such that one can see through it clearly.

trap.def: A machine or other device designed to catch (and sometimes kill) animals, either by holding them in a container, or by catching hold of part of the body.

treasure.def: A collection of valuable things; accumulated wealth; a stock of money, jewels, etc.

treaty.def: A formal binding agreement concluded by subjects of international law, namely, states and international organizations; a convention, a pact.

trial.def: An occasion on which a person or thing is tested to find out how well they perform or how suitable they are.

trigger.def: To cause, to precipitate, to bring (something) about in response or as a result.

triumph.def: A conclusive success following an effort, conflict, or confrontation of obstacles; victory; conquest.

trivial.def: Ignorable; of little significance or value.

tutor.def: One who teaches another (usually called a student, learner, or tutee) in a one-on-one or small-group interaction.

typically.def: In an expected or customary manner.

unanimous.def: Sharing the same views or opinions, and being in harmony or accord.

underestimate.def: To estimate too low; to perceive (someone or something) as having a lower value, quantity, worth, etc., than what he/she/it actually has.

undergo.def: To experience; to pass through a phase.

undertake.def: To take upon oneself; to start, to embark on (a specific task etc.).

unearth.def: To uncover or find; to bring out from concealment

unfairly.def: In a manner that is unfair.

unfavourable.def: Serving to hinder or oppose; adverse, disadvantageous, inconducive, unsuitable.

unify.def: Cause to become one; make into a unit; consolidate; merge; combine.

unintentionally.def: Without meaning to, in an unintentional manner, not intentionally.

unique.def: Being the only one of its kind; unequaled, unparalleled or unmatched.

unlikely.def: Not likely; improbable; not to be reasonably expected.

unrest.def: A state of trouble, confusion and turbulence, especially in a political context; a time of riots, demonstrations and protests.

urge.def: A strong desire; an itch to do something.

utilize.def: Alternative spelling of utilise. [To make use of; to use.]

utter.def: Senses relating to expressing sounds, etc., or disclosing something

utterly.def: Completely; entirely; to the fullest extent.

vague.def: Not clearly expressed; stated in indefinite terms.

vandalize.def: American, Canadian, and Oxford British English standard spelling of vandalise.

vanish.def: To become invisible or to move out of view unnoticed.

vary.def: Not to remain constant: to change with time or a similar parameter.

vehemently.def: In a vehement manner; expressing with a strong or forceful attitude.

venture.def: A risky or daring undertaking or journey.

verdict.def: A decision on an issue of fact in a civil or criminal case or an inquest.

verify.def: To confirm or test the truth or accuracy of something.

versatile.def: Capable of doing many things competently.

vessel.def: A craft for transportation on or in water, air, or space.

viable.def: Able to be done, possible, practicable, feasible.

violate.def: To break or disregard (a rule or convention).

violently.def: To an intense degree; extremely; strongly; intensely.

virtuous.def: Full of virtue; having excellent moral character.

vital.def: Necessary to the continuation of life; being the seat of life; being that on which life depends.

voluntary.def: Done, given, or acting of one's own free will.

vulnerable.def: More or most likely to be exposed to the chance of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.

wage.def: An amount of money paid to a worker for a specified quantity of work, usually calculated on an hourly basis and expressed in an amount of money per hour.

warehouse.def: A place for storing large amounts of products. In logistics, a place where products go to from the manufacturer before going to the retailer.

weary.def: Having the strength exhausted by toil or exertion; tired; fatigued.

widespread.def: Affecting, or found throughout, a large area (e.g. the entire land or body); broad in extent; widely diffused.

will.def: One's independent faculty of choice; the ability to be able to exercise one's choice or intention.

willingly.def: Of one’s own free will; freely and spontaneously.

wise.def: Showing good judgement or the benefit of experience.

withdraw.def: To draw or pull (something) away or back from its original position or situation.

witness.def: One who sees or has personal knowledge of something.

worship.def: To reverence (a deity, etc.) with supreme respect and veneration; to perform religious exercises in honour of.

wrap.def: To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.

yell.def: To shout; holler; make a loud sound with the voice, especially to express intense emotions such as anger or excitement.

yield.def: To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

zone.def: Any given region or area of the world.
